name: At birth – cord blood
forWhom: Mother Rh negative or blood group O, or a previous baby with jaundice needing treatment

name: First 24 hours – low-sugar watch
forWhom: Small, big or preterm baby, or mother with diabetes (check at 2 hours, then before feeds)

name: Day 0–2 – baby of a mother with diabetes
Day 2–3 – newborn screening before going home
Day 1–14 – jaundice work-up
forWhom: Visible jaundice, or a high skin (TcB) reading

name: Sepsis screen – baby unwell
forWhom: Signs of infection, or mother with fever, prolonged leaking or foul-smelling liquor

name: Day 3–14 – baby of a mother with thyroid disease
forWhom: Mother with hypothyroidism or Graves’ disease (repeat at 2 weeks)

name: Day 7–14 – repeat newborn screening
forWhom: Preterm, low birth weight or sick baby, or first sample taken before 48 hours

name: After day 14 – prolonged jaundice
forWhom: Jaundice beyond 14 days (21 days in a preterm baby), or pale stools / dark urine

name: Week 3–6 – preterm baby: anaemia and bone check
forWhom: Born before 34 weeks or under 1.5 kg

name: Antenatal booking tests
forWhom: First antenatal visit (the HIV test needs its consent form and counselling)

name: 24–28 weeks
forWhom: Every pregnant woman (ICT only if Rh negative)

name: Before an operation
forWhom: Caesarean section or gynaecological surgery (the HIV test needs its consent)

name: 6–12 weeks after delivery – sugar test after GDM
forWhom: Mother who had diabetes in pregnancy

name: Recurrent pregnancy loss work-up
forWhom: Two or more pregnancy losses (ESHRE 2022) – the doctor decides when to test
about: Tests for the work-up after two or more pregnancy losses (ESHRE Recurrent pregnancy loss, 2022; RCOG Green-top Guideline 17, 2023). Antiphospholipid antibodies: lupus anticoagulant (before any heparin), anticardiolipin IgG and IgM, anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I (ESHRE: can be considered); a positive result counts only if it is positive again at least 12 weeks later. Thyroid: TSH and TPO antibodies. HbA1c (or a fasting sugar): the hospital's choice, for diabetes that may be present or uncontrolled – not a routine ESHRE or RCOG test; the doctor decides. Not in the package: parental karyotype of both partners, only on the doctor's decision after assessment (order it as "Another test"; the lab attaches the report, as a typed karyotype is refused by the PCPNDT check); tests for inherited thrombophilia (not advised routinely); and a pelvic ultrasound for the shape of the uterus (3D if available), which is a scan, not a lab test – book it separately.
